questions.q: In "Know words, readers and the job of copy Understand", which of these is a key idea?
o: Keep source notes for every fact you use.
Replace vague words such as 'many' or 'fast' with a number or a fact the client can prove.
Keep client files safe: strong passwords, backups, access only for those who need it.
Learn the terms: headline, body, call to action, benefit, feature, tone, brief.

questions.q: In "Explain how a copy job runs from brief to delivery Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Make three samples that match the kind of client you want, with the brief shown beside each.
Draft an outline with headings before any full text.

Replace vague words such as 'many' or 'fast' with a number or a fact the client can prove.

questions.q: In "Write a clear short piece to a standard Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Write three headline options and pick the one that is clear before it is clever.
Keep a simple list: contact, date, reply, next step.
A brief says who the reader is, the goal, the tone, the length, the deadline and the one action wanted.
Review your contact list each week and send a polite follow-up to anyone who has not replied after one week.

questions.q: In "Follow Canadian rules for advertising and messages Evaluate", which of these is a key idea?
o: Edit twice: first for meaning and order, then for spelling, grammar and punctuation.
Keep a time log on every job for a month so your hourly cost rests on real hours, not guesses.
Compare the tone of two ads and say which reader each is written for and how you can tell.
Add a working unsubscribe line to your email template.

questions.q: In "Price your work and check it pays Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: List every claim in your copy that needs proof, such as a price, a ranking or a result, and ask the client for the proof.
Calculate your effective hourly rate by dividing total income by total hours, including admin and unpaid time.
Collect sales tax once registered; check the small-supplier limit with the tax agency.
Name one reader in one line: who they are, what they want, what worries them.

questions.q: In "Run your practice for real and grow it Create", which of these is a key idea?
o: Do not copy other people's writing or images; use your own words or licensed material.
Ask questions before you write; a short call saves a rewrite.
At the end choose: stop, change or grow, and write a 12-month plan.
Write down who owns the copy and what the client may do with it. Check with a legal adviser for large deals.
